interviewQuestions.question: How would you assign a delivery partner when both restaurant prep time and partner availability are unpredictable?
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
I'd frame the two failure modes first: assign too early and the partner idles at the restaurant; assign too late and the delivery is slower than it needs to be because search-and-travel time stacks on top of prep time.

My approach is to predict restaurant-ready-time — from that restaurant's historical prep times, or a live signal the restaurant provides — and time partner search so the partner's estimated arrival lines up with food actually being ready. For restaurants with volatile prep times, I'd bias toward assigning later and accept slightly higher delivery latency over partner idle time, since idle partners hurt the whole marketplace, not just one order.

I'd close by noting this needs a feedback loop — comparing predicted vs actual ready-time per restaurant to keep the prediction honest over time.

**Testing:** whether you can reason about a two-sided timing problem instead of picking one fixed assignment-time rule.
interviewQuestions.subTitle: Timing delivery-partner assignment

interviewQuestions.question: How would refunds and partial refunds change the order state machine?
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
I'd point out that a full refund maps cleanly onto the existing CANCELLED state — the order never completes, money comes back. A partial refund is trickier because the order still completes (food was delivered) but one line item wasn't fulfilled as ordered, so it can't reuse CANCELLED without lying about what actually happened.

I'd add a distinct terminal state, something like DELIVERED_WITH_ADJUSTMENT, reachable from the partial-fulfillment event I'd already modeled (an item going out of stock mid-prep), and I'd keep a record of exactly which lines were refunded and why, since that's needed for both customer support and restaurant payout reconciliation.

I'd close by noting refunds shouldn't be a side effect bolted onto the Order class — a PaymentService should own the actual refund call and report back a status the order records.

**Testing:** whether you extend a state machine cleanly for a new real-world case instead of overloading an existing state.
interviewQuestions.subTitle: Refunds and the order state machine
